spec_features.evidence: models.py ModelClient.complete() builds a SHA-256 cache key over exact inputs, checks DiskCache.get(key) and returns a cached Completion (from_cache=True) before any API call (models.py ~lines 155-180); DiskCache.get/put implemented (models.py ~lines 78-101). run.py _is_complete()/_load_transcript skip completed cells (resumability) in _run_one_cell (run.py ~lines 67-72).
spec_features.notes: Both caching and resume are genuinely wired and short-circuit re-elicitation/re-querying.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Identical inputs are therefore never re-billed, and reruns are incremental.

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving up is itself a welfare-relevant behavior
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:339 gave_up = comp.text is not None and GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in comp.text; :341 stop_reason='give_up'; :359-360 if gave_up: break ends the rollout. GIVE_UP_SENTINEL defined :37 and described in SYSTEM_PROMPT :34.
spec_features.notes: Sentinel is detected, recorded as a stop reason, AND breaks the loop end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: caching avoids needlessly re-eliciting distress responses on reruns
spec_features.evidence: Same cache mechanism as above (models.py complete() returns cached Completion before calling provider). A cache hit skips re-querying the subject model, so distress responses are not re-elicited on reruns.
spec_features.notes: The DESIGN.md frames this welfare rationale; the code implements only the generic cache.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Identical inputs are therefore never re-billed, and reruns are incremental.

spec_features.spec_quote: the rollouts are the expensive, welfare-relevant part
spec_features.evidence: run.py separates run_rollouts (transcripts) from score_all (re-reads transcripts), both share the cached ModelClient; main_async toggles via do_rollouts/do_scoring and CLI --skip-rollouts/--skip-scoring (run.py ~lines 152-205). Resume via _is_complete avoids re-running rollouts.
spec_features.notes: Re-scoring with a different judge does not re-run rollouts; this is real wired behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Resume: completed cells (a finished transcript on disk) are skipped, never re-queried.

spec_features.spec_quote: Because this study deliberately induces distress-like states, the cache and resume logic are not just performance features — they prevent needless re-elicitation
spec_features.evidence: DiskCache short-circuit in models.py complete(); run.py _run_one_cell skips completed transcripts (_is_complete) and never re-queries them. Both run and prevent re-querying the subject.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism genuinely runs; welfare framing is only in DESIGN.md, code comments are performance-oriented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a crashed run resumes without re-querying completed cells.

spec_features.spec_quote: the instrument is measurement-only (it never trains or deploys models)
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:444). No code path performs or gates training/deployment; the absence of training code is not an implemented protective mechanism. The judge only scores (judge.py); nothing enforces a 'no train/deploy' invariant.
spec_features.notes: An absence of training is not an enforced welfare feature.

code_only_features.feature_name: atomic cache writes prevent corruption / wasted re-elicitation
code_only_features.evidence: models.py DiskCache.put writes to a .tmp file then tmp.replace(path) (atomic), so an interrupted run keeps cached subject responses usable on resume, avoiding re-querying the subject. (Counted under the caching minimization already; listed for the atomic-write detail.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: stores the result as JSON. Cache hits short-circuit the API call
